claims.text: ZrB2 specimens can be fabricated using spark plasma sintering.
SPS at approximately 30 MPa and 1800–1900 °C can densify single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed SPS treatment significantly lowers the ZrB2 densification temperature relative to conventional processing above 2300 °C.
SPS permits short, minutes-scale dwell times for processing ZrB2.
The proposed process uses approximately 30 MPa uniaxial pressure, 1800–1900 °C, and an inert environment.
The starting material is specified as sufficiently pure, submicron-to-micron ZrB2 powder with minimal surface oxide.
Rapid, localized Joule heating during SPS reduces porosity in ZrB2.
Concurrent electric field and pressure enhance mass transport during ZrB2 sintering.
SPS electric current lowers the activation energy for ZrB2 sintering.
SPS drives localized heating at ZrB2 particle interfaces.
Localized interfacial heating produces faster densification at lower temperature and a refined ZrB2 grain structure.
Reduced porosity provides fewer pathways for liquid plating bath ingress.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have comparable or superior density to conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have comparable or superior mechanical integrity to conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will contain fewer pores and suffer less plating-bath infiltration during long exposure.
Reduced plating-bath infiltration will mitigate eventual ZrB2 component failure.
Conventionally sintered or hot-pressed ZrB2 above 2300 °C has higher porosity and limited resistance to extended liquid-bath exposure.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to sufficiently pure submicron-to-micron ZrB2 powder processed below 2000 °C under inert conditions.
Acidic or corrosive plating baths may require protective measures beyond SPS densification.
Performance gains may vary with powder morphology, contamination, and processing scale.
